主要内容: The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) released data showing that retail trade, finance and insurance, and utilities were the leading contributors to the 2.1 percent increase in real GDP in the fourth quarter of 2019. Real value added for retail trade increased 7.4 percent, primarily due to an increase in other retail, including gasoline stations and nonstore retailers. Finance and insurance saw a 5.1 percent increase, with securities, commodity contracts, and investments being the largest contributors. Utilities increased 23.3 percent, mainly due to an increase in electric power generation. Nondurable goods manufacturing decreased 2.8 percent, reflecting declines in food and beverage, tobacco, and petroleum products. Other services, except government, decreased 1.6 percent, with repair and maintenance and personal services being the main contributors to the decline. Construction increased 1.4 percent, after a 2.1 percent decrease in the third quarter. Real gross output increased 1.1 percent in the fourth quarter, with the private services-producing sector contributing 1.7 percent, the private goods-producing sector decreasing 1.4 percent, and the government sector increasing 2.8 percent. Real GDP for the U.S. increased 2.3 percent in 2019, driven by growth in private goods- and services-producing sectors and the government sector. The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported that in the fourth quarter and year 2019, real GDP growth was widespread, with 20 of 22 industry groups contributing to the increase. Professional, scientific, and technical services; finance and insurance; and information were the leading contributors to the increase in real GDP in 2019. For professional, scientific, and technical services, real value added increased 5.5 percent in 2019, after increasing 5.2 percent in 2018. The 2019 increase primarily reflected increases in miscellaneous professional, scientific, and technical services as well as computer systems design. Finance and insurance increased 3.3 percent in 2019, after decreasing 1.9 percent in 2018. The 2019 increase followed two consecutive years of decline and primarily reflected an increase in insurance carriers and related activities. Information services increased 4.6 percent in 2019, after increasing 8.5 percent in 2018. The 2019 increase primarily reflected increases in data processing, internet publishing, and other information services as well as publishing industries.
